finding.claim: Stored subscriber callbackUrl is used as the target of a recurring blind POST with no scheme, host, port, or allowlist validation (blind SSRF, MEDIUM).
finding.source: callbackUrl body field of POST /subscribe (documented src/Jobs.java:12)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24 via URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe with callbackUrl body field
subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl) receives the value unchanged
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it without validation
client.send dispatches the POST; response body read but never returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No validation at store time (:13-14) or fetch time (:19-21): no scheme, host, port, or allowlist check. Redirects are not a bypass: client is HttpClient.newHttpClient() (:10), which does not follow redirects by default. The /subscribe route and its authentication are not in this repo, so reachability by an external attacker is unconfirmed. Rated MEDIUM because the response is not returned (blind SSRF); raise to HIGH if /subscribe is confirmed unauthenticated and externally reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none: no scheme, host, port, or allowlist check at store time (src/Jobs.java:13-14) or fetch time (src/Jobs.java:19-21). HttpClient.newHttpClient() at src/Jobs.java:10 does not follow redirects by default, so that is not a bypass.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches (src/Jobs.java:12-24) and no closing guard exists, but the only source is a comment documenting POST /subscribe (src/Jobs.java:12), and the route handler, its authentication, and its network exposure are not in this repo, so I cannot confirm that an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker controls callbackUrl.
